Brighton finish the season on their highest ever Premier League points total of 41 points and in 15th position. Whilst Burnley finish 10th on 54 points, level with Sheffield United.
Brighton clinch a 2-1 victory over Burnley on the final day of the season, after a second half strike from Connolly wrapped up the win. It was 1-1 at the break after goals from Bissouma and Wood. It took Brighton just five minutes to retake the lead, with Connolly holding off Long and slotting past Pope. Burnley had a goal ruled out, after Gudmundsson was adjudged to be blocking Ryan in an offside position, as Rodriguez headed home from a corner. Wood then went close for the Clarets, but ultimately the couldn't get the second goal and Brighton held on for the three points.

An entertaining contest between Leicester City and Chelsea ends all square at the King Power Stadium. The Blues took the lead early in the second half through a Antonio Rudiger header, but the home side rallied as Harvey Barnes equalised courtesy of a deflected strike before Ben Chilwell put them ahead. However, Rudiger notched his second of the game with a thumping header from a Mason Mount free-kick to restore parity. Leicester should have scored a third to regain their advantage, only for Jonny Evans to place a free header wide of the post, while Barnes also missed a sitter from close range, dragging his shot away from the net. On the balance of play it was a fair result, although not one either side would have wanted before the start of the contest.

Sheffield United clinch all three points at Selhurst Park, with a 1-0 victory over Palace after an own goal by Guaita. Palace had been the better side in the first half, with Benteke having a couple of good opportunities, but they couldn't find the breakthrough. They almost went down to 10 men, with Ward shown a straight red card for a late and high challenge on Stevens, but after a VAR review, the colour of the card was changed to yellow. The visitors responded through Dominic Calvert-Lewin before half-time, nodding home at the back post after Mason Holgate flicked on Lucas Digne's cross. Jordan Pickford was required to make a super reaction stop to deny Pablo Fornals' header, while in the second half Tom Davies and Anthony Gordon both missed good opportunities for the Toffees. A draw is probably the fair result, although it will suit Everton a lot more than David Moyes' men, who sit just one point above the relegation zone in 16th place.

Leicester City hold a 1-0 lead at the break in their Premier League clash against Burnley at Turf Moor. Harvey Barnes broke the deadlock in the 33rd minute as he latched on to a loose ball following a challenge by Dennis Praet on Jack Cork. Burnley have been below par in the final third and have been restricted to efforts from distance in their attempts to threaten Kasper Schmeichel's goal. Liverpool secure a deserved 2-0 win after Salah's late strike allowed the hosts to overcome a nervy ending. Liverpool - as we've come to expect - started brightly and quickly took the lead when Van Dijk steered Alexander-Arnold's corner beyond De Gear. From there, the hosts should have added to their lead but squandered numerous chances, while Wijnaldum and Firmino also had goals ruled out. United mustered little in response but could have equalised through Pereira's desperate lunge at the back post. The second half initially followed a similar pattern as Liverpool wasted plenty of opportunities to add to their lead, but United steadily grew into the game. Martial wastefully blasted over when clean through and Greenwood almost connected with a cross to equalise, but the away side couldn't find an equaliser and Salah wrapped up the contest with a late breakaway goal - earning Liverpool a 2-0 lead and yet another win.

Everton seal a much-needed 1-0 victory over Brighton courtesy of Richarlison's first-half strike, but the visitors will feel unlucky to leave empty-handed after pushing hard for an equaliser in the second half. Murray then came off the bench to miss two chances to level the scores inside the final 10 minutes, but Everton eventually managed to cling on for a hard-earned victory.

Manchester City hold onto their narrow advantage and take all three points from Everton thanks to a 2-1 victory. Mikel Arteta's first home match ends in the worst manner possible as Arsenal succumbed to a late comeback from Chelsea to fall to a 2-1 defeat. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang's opener put the Gunners ahead with a fine headed finish from close range, but the home side were not able to compound their advantage. It left them open in the second half where they struggled to create openings in the final third. The game turned when Jorginho did not receive a second booking for pulling back Matteo Guendouzi in the middle of the park. It was the midfielder there to capitalise on a horrendous mistake by Bernd Leno to notch Chelsea's equaliser. The German came for a Mason Mount free-kick and missed the ball entirely, allowing Jorginho to tap home. The Blues' confidence surged and they hit the home side on the counter as Tammy Abraham provided a cool finish to secure the three points - a perfect response to their defeat to Southampton last time out. If Arteta believed he had a challenge on his hands before his arrival, he will know that this Arsenal team is in dire need of improvement across the pitch. Frighteningly for the Gunners there does not seem to be an easy remedy at hand.

Wolves picked up late on with the introduction of Jimenez and Traore, but couldn't do enough to grab an equaliser.

Manchester City get back to winning ways in the Premier League with a 2-0 victory over Sheffield United at the Etihad Stadium. It was not a clean performance from the home side as they were at the mercy of VAR and luck in the contest. Lys Mousset had put the Blades ahead with a low strike, only to see the goal disallowed by VAR on a marginal offside call. The forward then missed a good opportunity in front of goal, poking wide of the post. City struggled for rhythm in the final third, but fortune was on their side as a pass destined for John Fleck struck referee Chris Kavanagh and rolled towards Kevin De Bruyne. He teed up Sergio Aguero to hammer home from inside the box, much to the fury of the visitors. De Bruyne notched the all important second goal to kill off the game, burying a low strike into the bottom-left corner following good work by Riyad Mahrez. Pep Guardiola will not have been thrilled with the performance, but it was good enough for the three points.

It's goalless at the break at St James' Park in the Premier League clash between Newcastle United and Crystal Palace. The Magpies have had the majority of the possession, but the best chances of the half fell to Palace in the final 10 minutes. Wilfried Zaha should have put his team ahead when he was played through, but he fired his effort straight at Martin Dubravka. Luka Milivojevic came inches away from placing a 25-yard strike from a free-kick into the top-right corner, only to see the ball drift wide of the post. Miguel Almiron and Florian Lejeune both saw efforts saved comfortably by Vicente Guaita as the home side have lacked quality in the final third in the opening period.

Southampton will be hopeful they can get their first back-to-back home wins since March here. The hosts have lost just one of their last 13 home games against Norwich in all competitions. However, Norwich seem to have partially solved their defensive issues - they've kept a clean sheet in two of their last three Premier League away games. Which side will gain the initiative in the fight for Premier League survival?
Southampton make just the one change from their 2-1 win over Watford here last Saturday. Long is chosen to partner Ings up front; Obafemi takes his place on the bench. Norwich name the same XI that drew with Arsenal. Tettey is available again after missing that game for personal reasons.

Chelsea secure a 2-1 victory over Watford at Vicarage Road, but it should've been more as they had several chances to extend their lead. They led 1-0 at the break through Abraham and Pulisic doubled their lead at the start of the second period, his fourth goal in two Premier League games. Mount and Abraham also went close to scoring for the Blues, but they couldn't get beat Foster for the third time. Watford then pulled one back late on as Deulofeu was brought down in the penalty area and VAR awarded a penalty, after the referee originally turned down his appeals. The winger converted the subsequent penalty. Kepa then had to deny Foster right at the end of the game, to make it five league wins on the bounce for Chelsea.

Leicester go into second place in the table as they equal the biggest ever win in the Premier League. Their attention now turns to the EFL Cup when they face Burton Albion on Tuesday. The Foxes led 5-0 at the break through goals from Chilwell, Tielemans, Vardy and a brace from Perez, with Southampton going down to 10 men just 12 minutes into the game. If this were the United of old, you'd be reasonably confident of an away victory. United have won six of their last eight Premier League games away to Norwich, with their last two visits resulting in 1-0 wins. However, Norwich are a more entertaining outfit these days, especially at Carrow Road. They've scored 23 of their last 25 Premier League goals here. Don't bank on this being a bore.
Norwich boss Daniel Farke names an unchanged side from the one that kept a first clean sheet of the season in a 0-0 draw against Bournemouth last week. There's only one change to Man Utd's last Premier League starting line-up against Liverpool as they revert to a 4-2-3-1. Martial comes in for Rojo.

Everton secure a huge win over West Ham United to move out of the relegation zone courtesy of strikes from Bernard and Gylfi Sigurdsson, easing the pressure on Marco Silva in the process. Bernard put them ahead in the 17th minute with a fine finish from a tight angle after the opening looked to have gone. The Toffees pressed throughout the game and were unfortunate as Richarlison was denied by the post, while Theo Walcott struck the bar. Yerry Mina then saw a header controversially disallowed by the referee after an apparent infringement in the box. Jordan Pickford was then called into action to deny Angelo Ogbonna from close range, but then Gylfi Sigurdsson emerged from the bench to curl a stunning effort into the top left corner to ice the game. It's a huge moment in the campaign for Everton to stop a run of four-straight defeats, while West Ham are now winless in their last three matches.

Well, we've had a tight half in this game so far. Burnley had the better chances in the opening 25 minutes, with Wood causing plenty of problems in particular. However, Everton grew into the period and were slightly unlucky not to go ahead after creating a number of scrappy chances from corners. The main talking point of the half though, was Coleman's challenge on Pieters. The Everton right-back put in a dangerous-looking challenge on the Burnley man's ankle and was fortunate not to see a red card - much to the anger of the crowd at Turf Moor.

There goes the full-time whistle! Norwich crumbled at home against their fellow newly-promoted side. The home side were 5-0 ahead after 18 minutes as strikes from David Silva, Sergio Aguero, Riyad Mahrez, Bernardo Silva and Nicolas Otamendi put them in complete control. The onslaught stopped for a period before Bernardo Silva notched his second and third goals in the second half, earning a fine hat-trick. Kevin De Bruyne rounded off the scoring with a super strike into the left top corner, completing a brilliant performance from the Belgian and from Pep Guardiola's men. Quique Sanchez Flores's side suffered their worst defeat in the Premier League and are looking like a side in danger of relegation to the Championship. The Spaniard has a huge challenge on his hands to turn the team around.

Arsenal complete a terrific comeback to beat Aston Villa 3-2, despite being behind for much of the game and they went down to 10 men at the end of the first half. Villa led 1-0 at the break and went close to doubling their lead, before Arsenal won a penalty after Guendouzi was fouled by Engels and Pepe stepped up to convert it. However, it took Villa just 90 seconds to go ahead again, with Wesley finishing at the near post to make it 2-1. The Gunners then threw everything at their opponents, who dropped deeper and deeper and Arsenal finally got their reward late on, with Chambers scoring the equaliser, before Aubameyang scored a superb free-kick to clinch all three points for the hosts.

Arsenal could have gone third with a win but can have no complaints whatsoever with a point, and Watford may well feel they should have won it.
--- 90’ +4 Full time FULL-TIME: WATFORD 2-2 ARSENAL ---
(90’) Arsenal have eight men back defending, and eventually Cleverley commits a foul trying to win a header from Janmaat's cross. That might just do it.
--- 90’ +1 Highlight Watford almost win it at the death! Doucoure has come alive in the last 20 minutes. He drives forward wonderfully, taking the ball from box to box before spreading it wide to Sarr on the right. Sarr finds Doucoure with a great low ball, but the midfielder's side-footed finish is straight at Leno. Brilliant play from Doucoure, but that should have been 3-2! ---
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card Capoue goes into the book late on for a late challenge. Étienne Capoue ---
(90’) Out of nowhere, Pepe and Aubameyang look to be clear on goal but the latter is just crowded out before he can pick out a pass or a shot. Watford defended that well in the end, but there must have been some hearts in mouths here at Vicarage Road!
(89’) Xhaka does well to beat one man in midfield but his pass out to the right is lazy and Watford counter. Doucoure has a shot from the edge of the area, but it's quickly charged down and we're into four minutes of added-on time.
(88’) That might have been the chance for Arsenal! Maitland-Niles stands the ball up towards the back post from the right, Xhaka is unmarked but it's just out of reach and he can only toe it behind for a goal-kick. If he could have controlled that, he would have had plenty of time to pick out a finish.
(87’) Arsenal win a free-kick just inside the Watford half and Xhaka delivers it to the edge of the area, but it's cleared easily and Watford look to mount another assault. This is absolutely breathless!
(86’) The initial corner is cleared but Watford win it back immediately once again. The chance is wasted this time, though, Janmaat opting to shoot left-footed from a position to the right some 20 yards out and getting it horribly wrong. It flies well over, and Arsenal can breathe.
(85’) Another shooting opportunity for Watford. Doucoure does brilliantly with a swerving run in from the left touchline, the ball eventually comes to Cleverley at the edge of the area but his shot deflects behind off the head of Luiz. It might have been going over anyway, but Watford get a corner.
(84’) Watford are all over Arsenal here. The away side try to hold onto possession in their own half but Torreira is immediately pressed off the ball.
--- 83’ Highlight So close for Watford! Femenia crosses from the right, Pereyra misses an overhead kick, another Watford player swings a boot at it and it breaks for Deulofeu over on the left. He shoots right-footed but, for what seems like the fifth time in this second half, bends it just wide of the far post. Arsenal are on the ropes! ---
(82’) Capoue finds Femenia with a sensational cross-field ball over to the right, and the Spaniard controls it well. Watford are patient in their build-up and eventually Pereyra looks to bend in a cross from the right, which Luiz heads clear.
(81’) As you might imagine, Flores looks delighted, and he could end up being even happier. On the balance of this second half, it would take a brave shout to rule Watford out of winning this game from here.
--- 81’ Goal! GOAL! IT'S ALL SQUARE AT 2-2! Pereyra steps up calmly and rolls the ball into the bottom-left corner with Leno going the other way. Roberto Pereyra ---
--- 78’ Highlight Penalty to Watford! Arsenal go close through Torreira at one end but Watford break and Luiz brings down Pereyra right on the edge of the area! Pereyra will take it... ---
--- 78’ Substitution A final set of fresh legs for Watford. Janmaat replaces Holebas. Daryl Janmaat Jose Holebas ---
--- 76’ Yellow card Arsenal look worried here. There's still a full quarter of an hour to play and Leno is already booked for time-wasting from the free kick. Bernd Leno ---
(75’) The corner from the right is fairly simply cleared but Arsenal make a mess of the counter and the ball comes back in towards Sarr. There's some fairly panicked defending going on, but this time they do manage to work the ball clear before Cleverley catches Luiz late and gives away a foul.
(74’) Sarr looks to take matters into his own hands, leading an attack which threatens to stagnate 30 yards from goal. He gets the ball back from a team-mate and shoots, with his effort deflected straight behind for a corner.
(73’) Watford come forward down the left, Deulofeu shoots right-footed, held by Leno. Wash, rinse, repeat.
--- 71’ Highlight Nelson almost makes an impression straight after coming on! Maitland-Niles combines with Pepe over on the right, with the latter finding Nelson with a pass to the edge of the area. He shoots hard and low first time, but it's too close to Foster, who falls on the ball. ---
--- 71’ Substitution Ozil caused Watford problems in the first half, but he's struggled to make an impression in the second with the home side taking the initiative. He's replaced by the more mobile Nelson. Reiss Nelson Mesut Özil ---
(69’) Sarr looks to make an impression, popping up in that left-wing spot where Watford are targeting Maitland-Niles. He mistimes his run and is caught just offside.
(68’) Kabasele gets his head to the corner at the back post, but can't get it on target under pressure. It balloons harmlessly behind, and Arsenal have a goal kick - which Leno again sends long.
(67’) Arsenal are having to defend in numbers now, but the end result is still the same. Deulofeu gets the ball on the left, beats Maitland-Niles infield but can't find the far corner with his shot. There must have been a touch on this one, as Watford get a corner over on the right.
--- 67’ Substitution Emery looks to introduce some bite into his midfield, with Torreira replacing Guendouzi. Lucas Torreira Matteo Guendouzi ---
(65’) Femenia continues to threaten down the right and this time fires in a good low ball to Pereyra eight yards out. He looks to flick it toward the far post but just can't quite get enough of a connection.
--- 64’ Highlight A first chance for the substitute Sarr. He collects the ball from Deulofeu's pass in the middle of the penalty area, holding off Luiz' challenge well to spin and shoot, but he drags it across goal and wide. A difficult chance under pressure but he did well enough with the turn that you might have expected him to score. ---
(63’) Leno seems to learn his lesson and goes long with a goal kick, to ironic cheers from the crowd. Dawson wins the defensive header, but Arsenal fans would surely rather see them lose the ball 80 yards from goal than 18.
--- 63’ Substitution Second change of the afternoon from Flores, Hughes going off for Pereyra. Roberto Pereyra Will Hughes ---
(62’) Deulofeu is in behind again, jinking in between Luiz and Maitland-Niles, but Guendouzi is there to turn his attempted square ball behind for a corner.
(61’) Aubameyang has a crack from range, but he doesn't make a good connection with his right foot and it slithers harmlessly wide to the left of goal.
(60’) Arsenal are consistently giving themselves problems from goal kicks, and perhaps it isn't surprising. Since the start of last season, their players have made a combined 14 errors leading to opposition goals in the Premier League, at least two more than any other club in this time.
--- 60’ Substitution Arsenal make their first change, Willock coming on for Ceballos, who has had a pretty quiet game. Joseph Willock Daniel Ceballos ---
(59’) Femenia picks the ball up on the right once again - he's finding a lot of space over there - and, with the ball bobbling up slightly, he does what any sensible person would do and spanks it on the half-volley. It flies just over, but had Leno worried for a split second.
(57’) Watford go close again and, as has been a theme in this game, it's Deulofeu with the effort. He drifts in from the left and fires a right-footed shot towards the far bottom corner from the edge of the area, but he just doesn't get enough curve on the strike and it bounces wide.
(56’) Maitland-Niles makes headway down the right but checks back and can't pick out a dangerous ball. Watford break and though Arsenal do win the ball back, the home side press them well. This has turned into a good game!
--- 56’ Yellow card Kolasinac is pulled back on the halfway line by Femenia as Arsenal looked to build an attack down the left. Femenia gets a yellow for his trouble. Kiko ---
--- 54’ Substitution Summer signing Sarr comes on in the first change of the afternoon, replacing Gray. Ismaila Sarr Andre Gray ---
--- 53’ Assist Deulofeu gets the assist after stretching out a foot to intercept Sokratis' pass from the goal kick. Watford had been threatening from that exact position already in this half. Gerard Deulofeu ---
--- 53’ Goal! GOAL! CLEVERLEY PULLS ONE BACK, IT'S 2-1! Watford have pressed Arsenal really well from goal kicks, and this time Sokratis' pass to Guendouzi is intercepted by Deulofeu. He can't control it but it comes to Cleverley at the edge of the area, and the midfielder sweeps a low shot under Leno. Good finish. Tom Cleverley ---
(51’) Femenia picks up the ball in a similar position on the right and, with bodies in the box, floats a cross in toward the six-yard line. Sokratis heads as far as Doucoure who shoots left-footed, but he scuffs his shot badly and it spins away, wide to the left of goal.
(50’) Femenia finds some space over on the right again, as Watford work the play from side to side. He looks to find Deulofeu in behind with a reverse pass, but Ceballos does well to track him and shepherd it out for a goal kick.
(49’) Xhaka gets the ball a very long way from goal, is urged to shoot, and does so. He catches it reasonably well, but it flies high and wide. Emery presumably just lets him have one of those in every game.
(48’) Watford have lost five of their last six Premier League home games against Arsenal, and look like making it a sixth here. The outlier, though, did see them come from behind to win – a 2-1 victory back in October 2017, with Cleverley winning the game in stoppage time.
(47’) Arsenal have started the second half in fairly frantic fashion. They need to take a moment to get the game back under control, or they're playing right into Watford's hands as they seek an early goal.
(46’) Deulofeu comes in from the left and finds Hughes at the edge of the area. He swipes his left boot at it first time, but gets right underneath it and it goes a long way over the bar. Perfect field-goal technique, though.
(45’) Femenia instantly flies forward down the right flank and puts in what initially looks like a good low cross to the edge of the six-yard box. There's nobody attacking it, though, and Leno gathers easily.
(45’) We're back underway here, Watford getting the second half off and running. Have they got a comeback in them?
Watford have been far from terrible here but they need to find a way of threatening other than Deulofeu's dribbling. Aside from that, they've looked blunt, and Arsenal have dealt with everything they've thrown at them fairly easily.
A slightly unusual half, all told. Watford have had the ball in more dangerous areas but haven't really looked like scoring, while Arsenal haven't done a huge amount of anything but scored two lovely goals. Aubameyang has them both thanks to one excellent finish and one back-post tap-in, with the two full-backs Kolasinac and Maitland-Niles claiming an assist each.
--- 45’ +3 Half time HALF-TIME: WATFORD 0-2 ARSENAL ---
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card Holebas sees yellow as well for his part in the scuffle, but he's not happy about it. Jose Holebas ---
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card Holebas and Pepe butt heads after a coming-together, Guendouzi comes and gets involved, and there's a scuffle over on the right touchline. Guendouzi had just had a talking-to from the referee, and he's booked for racing into the affray. Matteo Guendouzi ---
(44’) Every time Watford look like scoring, it's Deulofeu involved. Gray wins a good header from a throw-in over on the left, Deulofeu drives at the Arsenal defence and looks to finish left-footed, but in the end he just runs out of pitch and ends up in a heap.
(43’) Holebas takes the free-kick left-footed, and curls it straight into Leno's waiting gloves. Watford should have made something of that, the free-kick was in an awkward position to the right of the penalty area.
--- 43’ Yellow card Luiz gives Maitland-Niles a job to do with a high pass out to the right-back, and Deulofeu robs him of the ball. Watford work the ball over to Hughes on the right, and Kolasinac slides in on him late. He gets the first yellow card of the afternoon. Sead Kolasinac ---
(40’) Ozil again pops up on the right, but this time the pass towards him is heavy and he can't keep it in play. With Pepe and Aubameyang ahead of him, there might have been an opportunity to kill the game off there, if the pass into Ozil had been more measured.
(39’) The corner is fairly easily dealt with and Ozil looks to carry the ball away down the left, but he is hounded by Deulofeu and passes it out of play. Arsenal eventually regroup and take control of possession again.
(38’) Cleverley feeds the ball behind for Doucoure, making a run infield from the right touchline, but Xhaka is there to snuff out the danger and stab it out for a corner.
(37’) Hughes cuts back and attempts a left-footed cross from the right, but Sokratis powers a header clear. The away side haven't looked too troubled by Watford's crossing game today, with Troy Deeney badly missed.
(36’) Aubameyang's second today was a vintage Arsenal goal. There were 20 passes in the build-up - the longest passing sequence leading to a goal in the 2019-20 Premier League season so far.
--- 35’ Highlight A chance for Watford! Guendouzi is caught out by Gray and Deulofeu at the edge of his own area from a goal kick, and the Spaniard shoots. Leno can only parry it out to a yellow shirt and another shot comes in, but this time it's wide to the right of the goal. ---
(34’) Hughes attempts a first-time side-footed finish from Femenia's cross from the right, but he scuffs it slightly and it goes wide of the near post.
(33’) Deulofeu and Cleverley combine well around the penalty area as Watford look to hit back, but the former can't find a shooting angle and the latter's cross towards the far post is cleared away.
(33’) Again, the goal came somewhat out of nowhere but the visitors have just made their extra quality show when it has mattered. A difficult half-time team talk for Flores lies ahead.
--- 32’ Assist Maitland-Niles put it on a plate for Aubameyang and gets the assist, but real credit to Ozil for the pass into him. Lovely stuff from Arsenal again. Ainsley Maitland-Niles ---
--- 32’ Goal! GOAL! Aubameyang again, it's 2-0! Ozil plays a lovely pass in behind for Maitland-Niles on the right, he fires the ball in low and Aubameyang is on hand to tap it in at the back post. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang ---
(29’) Holebas bends in a cross from close to the left byline. There's a nice shape and power on the ball in, but the Arsenal defence deal with it and it's headed away from danger.
(27’) Ozil is spending a lot of time out by the right touchline, and Watford are struggling to deal with the German out there alongside Maitland-Niles and Pepe. They look like they've identified that left-back area as a potential weak spot in the home side today.
(26’) Xhaka gets a good foot in as Watford look to build an attack. The home side have generally had the more threatening possession in this game so far but with Pepe and Aubameyang up front, there is always the risk of a counter from the Gunners.
--- 25’ Highlight Inches away! Ozil rolls the ball into a dangerous area from the right of the penalty area, and Aubameyang just can't get the final touch. Kabasele got a slight deflection on the ball which might just have saved his side there. ---
(24’) Watford looked a little rattled straight after the goal, Arsenal winning the ball back almost immediately, but they're putting their foot on the ball and holding onto it for the moment. Is there a response on the way?
(22’) Arsenal haven't exactly been on top here, but those moments can be the difference in these games. Aubameyang has been just lethal this season. Only Mohamed Salah (53) has been involved in more Premier League goals since Aubameyang’s debut for Arsenal in February 2018 (45; 36 goals, 9 assists).
--- 21’ Assist Kolasinac gets a good assist. He helped win the ball on halfway, and made a good run forward before delaying the pass to Aubameyang well. Sead Kolasinac ---
--- 21’ Goal! GOAL! 1-0 ARSENAL! One chance is all Aubameyang needs! Arsenal win the ball on the half-way line, Kolasinac drives forward and finds Aubameyang in a pocket of space at the edge of the area. He controls brilliantly, spins and pokes it into the bottom-left corner with his right foot. Great goal. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang ---
(20’) Pepe gets the ball in a similar position on the right and this time looks to slide the ball across the line of the penalty area, but his ball is easily cut out.
(19’) Guendouzi does well to control a risky dinked pass at the edge of his own area and Arsenal break upfield. Pepe gets the ball on the right, drifts infield and looks to shoot towards the far post with his left foot, but it floats a yard or so wide. Foster didn't look too concerned.
(18’) Again, the Arsenal defenders back off Deulofeu - they seem scared to commit in case he gets past them. This time, he opts to pass and Watford work the ball out to Hughes on the right, but the attack breaks down.
(17’) Ceballos tricks his way into the area, just to the left of the D and tries to chip a little pass into Aubameyang. The ball is intercepted in a crowd, though, and the home side can clear.
(15’) Watford win a corner over on the left. The delivery looks a fairly threatening one, right into a crowded six-yard box, but a free-kick eventually goes to Arsenal. There's plenty of pushing and shoving in there but it looks like an accidental handball from Kabasele.
(14’) Arsenal play the ball from left to right, Ozil finds Pepe in space to play a low ball into the area but it's cleared fairly easily. Still no clear-cut chances for the away side here.
(13’) Deulofeu is causing all sorts of problems for Maitland-Niles on the left wing. He beats him inside the area and plays the ball back for Holebas, who fires well over from the edge of the box when he should probably do better. He looked caught in two minds between power and placement and ended up with neither.
(12’) Watford are looking to avoid an unwanted milestone here today. They haven’t lost their opening three home league matches of a season since the 1991-92 campaign – the Hornets won their opening three at Vicarage Road last season.
(11’) The corner is cleared but it drops to Deulofeu over on the left flank. He plays the ball inside for Cleverley to shoot again, but his curling effort towards the bottom-right corner is easily saved this time.
--- 10’ Highlight Good effort from Cleverley! He finds a pocket of space at the edge of the area with Luiz backing off. He unleashes a rasping right-footed drive at goal which Leno does well to tip over for a corner over on the right side. ---
(9’) Gray threatens to combine with Cleverley, but there's a heavy touch from the former and he ends up fouling Kolasinac just inside the centre circle.
(7’) Ozil looks towards the back post, but Dawson is there to head clear and Arsenal will look to build from the back again. Ceballos finds Ozil with a nice lofted pass out to the right touchline, but the away side are happy to play it around in midfield for the time being.
(6’) Maitland-Niles puts in a low cross which looks to be put behind for a corner, but Holebas catches him late. It looks a fairly painful one but the right-back is up on his feet and Ozil has a free-kick to deliver, to the right of the penalty area.
(6’) Deulofeu drifts in from the left and curls a right-footed shot towards the far post, but Leno claims it easily enough after a slight fumble. He had Holebas overlapping on that left wing, and the Greek may well have been the better option.
(5’) Luiz gets a foot in as Hughes looks to fire in a low cross from the right. No big chances to speak of in the first five minutes, but this looks set up to be a good game.
(4’) Dawson attempts a ball over the top for Gray to chase, but his pass has too much on it and this time Leno watches it behind. The Arsenal back four were positioned fairly deep, so the pass would have to have been inch-perfect.
(3’) Pepe and Aubameyang look to combine for the first time, the former playing a disguised pass in behind, but it's overhit and Foster can watch it out for a goal-kick.
(2’) Kabasele attempts a switch of play but it's intercepted by Kolasinac, who drives forward and looks to set Pepe free down the right. Dawson does well to slide and intercept.
(1’) Arsenal enjoy a bit of possession to start the game off, as you might have expected. They're probing from left to right, feeling out Watford's set-up. Deulofeu does well to rob the ball in midfield and gets past one man down the left, but is then tackled.
We're off! Aubameyang gets the ball rolling, as Flores accepts a warm reception from the home fans. He's clearly still liked here, and it's a lovely afternoon for his first game back.
Right then! The stage is set, the sun is shining, and the players are on their way out of the tunnel. A new manager boost for Watford, or back to winning ways for Arsenal?
The Gunners will be confident going into this one, having won each of their last three Premier League games against the Hornets without conceding a goal. Watford were, in fact, the only side not to score against Arsenal in the Premier League last season.
There's no Alexandre Lacazette for Arsenal today. He's apparently been playing on an injured ankle for the last few games, but is now expected to be out until October as it heals.
So, Flores makes three changes from Gracia’s final starting eleven with Holebas, Capoue and Deulofeu the men to come in. Ozil gets his first Gunners appearance of the season, after scoring in last season’s 2-0 win over Watford at the Emirates.
SUBS: Emiliano Martinez, Calum Chambers, Lucas Torreira, Joe Willock, Reiss Nelson, Gabriel Martinelli, Bukayo Saka.
ARSENAL (4-3-3): Bernd Leno; Sead Kolasinac, David Luiz, Sokratis, Ainsley Maitland-Niles; Granit Xhaka, Matteo Guendouzi, Dani Ceballos; Mesut Ozil, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Nicolas Pepe.
SUBS: Heurelho Gomez, Daryl Janmaat, Adrian Mariappa, Nathaniel Chalobah, Ismaila Sarr, Dimitri Foulquier, Roberto Pereyra.
WATFORD (4-2-3-1): Ben Foster; Jose Holebas, Craig Dawson, Christian Kabasele, Kiko Femenia; Etienne Capoue, Abdouaye Doucoure; Gerard Deulofeu, Tom Cleverley, Will Hughes; Andre Gray.
Watford are, of course, going back to the future in their first game following the sacking of Javi Gracia. Quique Sanchez Flores is back in the hotseat but with Arsenal looking good at times this season, he could be in for a difficult first day back on the job.
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Watford against Arsenal at Vicarage Road. Kick-off is set for 16:30 local time, so stick with us for live commentary, stats and analysis throughout the game!

The point lifts Villa out of the bottom three, while West Ham are now on eight points, though they failed to take their chance to move up into the top three.
It’s honours even at Villa Park, as West Ham hang on with 10 men. Neither of those stoppage-time penalty shouts were worthy of spot-kicks and, ultimately, in a game of few clear-cut chances a draw is a fair result.
--- 90’ +4 Full time FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 WEST HAM. ---
--- 90’ +3 Highlight Now West Ham want a penalty! Fredericks got clear down the right and charged into the area, with Mings forced into what looked to be a desperate lunge. He gets away with it, though. ---
--- 90’ +2 Highlight NO PENALTY! West Ham fail to clear the corner and after a bit of pinball it falls to Wesley. He looks all set to fire home, but instead collapses to the ground six yards out. Appeals go up from the crowd, but the referee is unmoved. ---
--- 90’ +1 Substitution West Ham have made a change. Noble going off with centre-back Balbuena coming on. Fabian Balbuena Mark Noble ---
(90’) There will be a minimum of three minutes added on. As the board goes up, Taylor plays in a cross which Ogbonna clears, though only out for a corner.
(89’) Huge cries of frustration from the home fans. Wesley finds himself in space, but only gets off a tame shot which does not test Fabianski at all.
--- 88’ Highlight CHANCE! That should have been the winner for Villa! Douglas Luiz delivers a fine cross which leaves West Ham’s defence helpless. Grealish had made a well-timed run to get on the end of it, but can’t adjust his feet quickly enough to connect with his volley. ---
(87’) Since their return to the Premier League in 2012-13, West Ham have picked up 22 red cards in the competition, with only Newcastle managing more in that time.
--- 85’ Substitution Smith makes his final change, with Davis replacing Guilbert. Keinan Davis Frédéric Guilbert ---
(84’) Clever, experienced play from Noble. West Ham got themselves stuck on the edge of Villa’s area, but Fornals spotted his captain in space. The midfielder took it down, only for his touch to force him wide, but he got his body in front of  Guilbert to win a foul.
(83’) Douglas Luiz is quickly involved. First, he gets his foot on the ball as Villa work it down the right, only for El Mohamady’s looping cross to be cleared. West Ham counter, with the former Manchester City player conceding a rather reckless foul on Haller.
--- 81’ Substitution Smith makes a second change. Nakamba, who has had a solid enough debut, makes way for Douglas Luiz. Douglas Soares Marvelous Nakamba ---
(80’) West Ham have, if anything, looked the more dangerous side since they were reduced to 10 men. Fornals finds himself with plenty of time on the ball and elects to shoot from around 25 yards out, forcing Taylor into a block which deflects it wide for a corner. The visitors cannot make anything of it, however.
(79’) That is extremely poor from El Mohamady! Wesley did well to play a quick one-two with his team-mate and take Zabaleta out of the game. The Brazilian charges down the right, and El Mohamady had acres of space to either drive forward or play a pass towards the striker. Instead, he plays a negative pass back to Guilbert who, under pressure from Haller, lumps a dreadful attempted ball to Taylor out of play.
--- 77’ Yellow card The visiting Hammers are happier with the referee now. Mings has gone into the book, having lead with his arm when challenging Haller. Tyrone Mings ---
(76’) The West Ham fans have been quick to air their displeasure at Mike Dean’s decision. “It’s all about you,” they’re chanting at the referee. Meanwhile, Villa are looking to pick the lock, but Grealish overhits a cross and West Ham easily see it out of play.
(75’) Referee Mike Dean has now awarded 102 red cards in the Premier League.
--- 74’ Highlight This match has come alive again! West Ham launch a counter, with Haller managing to get a snapshot off in the area, but it does not get through a crowd of defenders. ---
(72’) McGinn presses high and steals the ball off Zabaleta, immediately looking to find a team-mate with a raking cross. Wesley gets underneath it, but El Ghazi manages to get there, though he can only turn it towards Grealish, who cannot take it under his spell.
(71’) Masuaku is the first West Ham player to be sent off in the Premier League since Noble against Leicester City in October last year.
--- 69’ Substitution Well, Pellegrini – who has turned 66 today – has now been forced into a change. Felipe Anderson, West Ham’s most likely goal threat so far, has made way for Zabaleta. Pablo Zabaleta Felipe Anderson ---
--- 67’ Red card! RED CARD! Masuaku is off! It is an incredibly harsh decision from Mike Dean, but VAR cannot review a yellow-card offence. Masuaku dived in on El Mohamday, but hardly made any contact. The referee had made his mind up, however, with West Ham's protests falling on deaf ears. Arthur Masuaku ---
--- 66’ Substitution Smith has reacted to West Ham’s change with a substitution of his own. El Mohamady, a full-back by trade, is on in place of Jota, who had faded since the restart. Ahmed El Mohamady Jota ---
(65’) After a spell of Villa pressure, West Ham have managed to gain a foothold now, with Lanzini and Noble getting on the ball in midfield. Haller eventually drops in to spread it wide to Felipe Anderson, who aims to pick out the striker with a flat cross, but it soars out of play.
--- 62’ Substitution Here’s a first change, and it is Pellegrini who blinks first. Yarmolenko is indeed the one who makes way, with former Villarreal playmaker Fornals coming on in his place, and the Spain Under-21 international should inject some more pace and energy into West Ham's attack. Pablo Fornals Andriy Yarmolenko ---
(61’) Great work from Nakamba, who has certainly grown into the game after a difficult first half. The midfielder tracked Masuaku’s run and did well to steward the full-back out of play, preventing the cross and earning a goal-kick.
(59’) El Ghazi is played in by McGinn, but his shot is easily saved by Fabianski. West Ham conceded possession easily, though, but Taylor fails to maintain the Villa pressure. The home crowd are in good voice now and sense their team have the upper hand.
(57’) Excellent defending from Grealish! The Villa playmaker has excelled in his box-to-box role under Smith, and the youngster just made a wonderful block to deny Rice. Haller had laid it off to the England international, but Grealish was out quickly to make a block.
(55’) Grealish won five fouls in the first half - he has now been fouled 18 times in the Premier League this season, a joint league high, alongside Wilfried Zaha. He could have just won another, having been barged into on the edge of West Ham's area, but the referee waves play on.
--- 52’ Highlight A clever turn from Grealish sees him spin away from two markers and Villa’s playmaker then has some space to run into in front of West Ham’s defence. Chelsea return to action in a week's time with a home match against another promoted club as they welcome Sheffield United to Stamford Bridge. As for Norwich, they travel to West Ham next Saturday after first taking on Crawley Town in the EFL Cup second round.
Chelsea beat Norwich 3-2 at Carrow Road to pick up their first win of the Lampard era. The visitors were made to work hard for the victory, with their opponents twice pegging them back in the first half. Cantwell cancelled out Abraham's early strike and Pukki did likewise after Mount restored his side's lead, but Abraham scored the only goal of the second half to give his Chelsea career lift-off. Rudiger thought he had scored a fourth goal for Lampard's charges, but it was ruled out for an infringement in the build-up.

Games at St. Mary's are rarely found wanting for goals. Southampton have both scored and conceded in 13 of their last 14 Premier League home fixtures, with the exception being a 2-0 win against Fulham in February.
This is the third meeting between Ralph Hasenhuttl and Jurgen Klopp in all competitions - Klopp has won both of the previous two, the first with Borussia Dortmund against VfR Aalen in the DFB-Pokal in October 2012 and the second with Liverpool - a 3-1 win against Southampton last season.
Liverpool have only lost one of their last 11 Premier League meetings with Southampton (W7 D3), losing 3-2 in March 2016, and have won their last four league meetings, scoring 11 goals and conceding just once in this run. However, the Reds had lost five of their previous seven against Saints prior to this.
Jurgen Klopp is boosted by Adrian's swift return to fitness following a collision with a pitch-invading fan following their Super Cup victory in Istanbul, and he starts in between the sticks ahead of emergency signing Lonergan, with first-choice stopper Alisson still out with a calf problem. The German still makes two changes, however, with Firmino and Alexander-Arnold starting ahead of Henderson and Gomez. Naby Keita is sidelined with injury and does not make the squad.
Southampton boss Ralph Hasenhuttl makes one change from the side that was beaten by Burnley last time out, dropping former Liverpool striker Ings to the bench in favour of an extra central midfielder in Hojbjerg as he looks for more solidity from his team. Liverpool kick off their 2019-20 Premier League campaign with a resounding 4-1 win over Norwich at Anfield. All four of the hosts' goals came in a dominant first-half showing as Salah, Van Dijk and Origi found a way through after Hanley had put into his own net early on. Klopp lost Alisson to an apparent calf injury late in the first half, though, and he will not be all that pleased with the defensive showing of his side as they were caught out on a few occasions by Norwich, who pulled one back through Pukki 64 minutes in. Still, a three-goal victory on the opening day is not a bad way to start the new season!

Arsenal clinch a 1-0 victory over Newcastle in their first league game of the season, thanks to a 58th-minute goal from Aubameyang. It was a game with very few chances, especially in the second half, with Newcastle unable to test Leno in the Gunners goal during the second period. Arsenal broke the deadlock when Maitland-Niles did well to nick the ball off the toes of Willems, he then raced forward and whipped the ball into the box for Aubameyang, who chipped the ball over Dubravka and into the back of the net.

Lampard's first match in charge of Chelsea in the Premier League ends in a painfully heavy defeat as Manchester United beat Chelsea 4-0. Rashford won a penalty and then put United ahead after confidently converting his spot-kick into the top-left corner. Then, two goals in two minutes in the second half took the game away from Chelsea as Martial fired in from close range before Rashford got his second after latching onto Pogba's brilliant pass.
